One room gets little air Book soon

Likely causes

  • A duct is crushed or sharply bent.
  • Furniture blocks the room opening.

Check safely first

  • Check that the room opening is unobstructed.
  • Compare airflow with a nearby room.

Air escapes through a visible seam Book soon

Likely causes

  • The connection has worked loose.
  • An old seal has peeled away.
  • The adjoining sections are poorly supported.

Check safely first

  • Observe the seam from a safe standing position.
  • Note when escaping air is strongest.
  • Leave the joint visible for inspection.

What the technician does

The technician checks joint fit and support before sealing. Suitable duct sealant or rated sealing tape addresses leakage once the connection is secure.

The number of leaking joints and their accessibility determine the scope.

A duct hangs loose or has disconnected Call today

Likely causes

  • A connection has pulled apart.
  • A support has failed.
  • Nearby work disturbed the branch.

Check safely first

  • Photograph the separation without moving the duct.
  • Identify which rooms have lost airflow.
  • Keep people and stored items away from the loose section.
  • Avoid climbing or reaching into a concealed opening.
  • Do not disturb old wrapped duct insulation or paper tape in an older building; leave it for assessment.

What the technician does

The technician checks both ends, restores the connection, and addresses support. Sealing cannot bridge a missing connection or support a loose run.

Reconnection may be limited work; damaged ends can require a replacement section.

When to act: Schedule prompt service for the affected rooms.

Flex duct is flattened or sharply bent Book soon

Likely causes

  • Stored items compressed the run.
  • A tight bend restricts the passage.
  • A sagging section has lost support.

Check safely first

  • Remove nearby movable items without touching the duct.
  • Note where the run appears flattened.
  • Do not cut or pull the outer covering.

What the technician does

The technician checks the inner passage and outer covering. Torn or permanently crushed sections may need replacement, with routing and support that prevent another restriction.

The damaged length and room to correct the route affect the work.

When to act: Arrange inspection rather than squeezing it back into shape.

Dust returns around room openings Book soon

Likely causes

  • A return joint draws air from an unintended space.
  • Dust has collected near an opening.
  • Household dust comes from another source.

Check safely first

  • Note which rooms collect dust most quickly.
  • Check whether furniture covers a return opening.
  • Record any recent building work.

What the technician does

The technician checks accessible return joints and other dust sources. Dust alone does not prove a duct defect, and repair cannot eliminate all household dust.

Tracing the entry point comes before choosing a repair.

Bills rise while rooms stay uneven Book soon

Likely causes

  • Supply air leaks before reaching the room.
  • A restricted branch delivers little air.
  • Weather or another system problem changed energy use.

Check safely first

  • Compare bills for similar weather periods.
  • List rooms that remain uncomfortable.
  • Note whether airflow changed suddenly.

What the technician does

The technician checks whether a duct fault explains the room pattern. Repair addresses confirmed leakage, but any bill change depends on other conditions.

Several small leaks can require more inspection than one visible break.

Ducts bang or rattle during operation Book soon

Likely causes

  • A loose section vibrates against its support.
  • Metal moves as pressure changes.
  • A restriction changes airflow through the run.

Check safely first

  • Note when the noise begins and stops.
  • Record the sound from an accessible room.
  • Observe visible movement without touching the run.
  • Do not wedge objects against the duct.

What the technician does

The technician separates loose connections from movement caused by airflow. Support may address vibration; pressure-related sounds call for investigation of the restriction.

Finding the source may take longer when sound travels through concealed runs.

When to act: Arrange service if the sound is new or worsening.

Likely causes

  • Persistent moisture affected the metal.

Residential duct repair questions

How are leaking or disconnected ducts actually repaired?

Repair starts at the joints. Loose connections are refastened with sheet metal screws, then sealed with mastic or UL 181 listed foil tape, never cloth duct tape. A supply branch that has pulled off its takeoff collar gets the collar re-secured, or a new collar where the old one is damaged. A fresh mechanical connection goes in either way. Torn or missing insulation is replaced so the sealed joint stays dry and quiet. City & Suburban has NATE-certified technicians, and the repair method should match the duct material and connection type. Sealing is a repair, not a rebuild. A run that is crushed or badly undersized along most of its length needs new duct instead.

How is a duct leak actually found?

By measurement, not by a glance. A useful assessment reads airflow and air temperature at the register in the room that is complaining, then compares them with a room that heats normally. It reads static pressure across the air handler as well, because a leaking return and a clogged filter move that number in opposite directions. The branch is then traced seam by seam until the gap, the dropped collar or the flattened length shows itself. A concealed run inside a wall chase or above finished plaster cannot be cleared by eye, so an access point has to be opened. City & Suburban diagnoses before quoting, which puts the readings ahead of the repair price rather than after it.

Why do far rooms in a two-flat or bungalow stay cold while the furnace runs?

Distance and leakage, usually in that order. Many two-flats, greystones and bungalows were ducted long after the frame went up. Branches travel through balloon-frame wall chases, panned floor joists and old gravity trunks never meant for a blower. Every unsealed seam on that path bleeds heated air into a basement, crawlspace or exterior wall before the register sees it. A front bedroom at the end of a long flex run loses most of its airflow this way. Airflow read at the registers shows which branch is losing its share. That weak branch is then traced back to the trunk it leaves.

Do duct leaks raise a heating bill enough to notice?

Leaks cost twice. Air that escapes a supply joint in an unheated basement never reaches a room. The thermostat then keeps the blower and burner running longer than the heat load requires. Return leaks are worse per square inch, because the system then pulls cold basement air back across the furnace and dilutes what every register delivers. Rental buildings feel this first. Where the landlord supplies heat, the Chicago Heat Ordinance applies. It sets a minimum of 68 degrees from 8:30 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. The overnight minimum is 66 degrees, and both apply between September 15 and June 1 (Municipal Code 13-196-410). A system fighting its own duct losses struggles to hold that in January.

Can crushed or kinked flex duct be repaired, or does it have to be replaced?

Flex duct fails by shape. A kink at a sharp turn, a length squashed behind stored boxes, or a long sagging span all throttle airflow. The duct can look intact from the outside. A crushed inner liner cannot be restored, so the damaged length is cut out and replaced. The new piece is pulled straight and carried on wide straps at the spacing the manufacturer specifies. A torn outer jacket is a smaller fix that can be sealed in place. A flattened section is replaced rather than taped back into shape, and the new run is kept as straight as the joist bays allow.

Does repairing ducts cut down on household dust?

Often yes, because return-side gaps pull unfiltered dust straight into the air stream. Gaps at a return plenum, an unsealed filter slot or a panned joist return draw in dust, loose fiberglass and crawlspace air. That load travels straight past the filter and spreads room to room. Sealing the return side is the part of duct repair that shows up on furniture and shelves. Duct repair belongs alongside filtration and humidity equipment as indoor air quality work. Cleaning the inside of a duct is a separate service and will not fix a leaking return.

How can a homeowner tell a duct fault from a furnace fault?

The pattern of the complaint points one way or the other. Heat that is weak in every room points at the equipment, the filter or the blower. So does a system that short cycles and trips its limit switch. Heat that is normal in some rooms and absent in others, with the furnace running fine, points at the duct path. Whistling at the cabinet, a thump when the blower starts and warm basement joists are duct signs. City & Suburban repairs both furnaces and ductwork, so the diagnosis decides the work. Equipment faults are handled as heater repair rather than duct repair.

What happens on a duct repair visit, and how long does it take?

A useful duct repair visit starts in the room that is complaining and works back along its branch. Readings at the register and at the air handler should set the scope before anything is opened. How long the visit takes depends on access and the number of joints opened. On an exposed basement or crawlspace run, sealing seams, re-securing a dropped branch and swapping flex are reachable repairs. Work behind finished plaster, or a fitting that must be fabricated for an odd gravity trunk, may need a second trip. City & Suburban gives a written price before the work, and same-day appointments are available when the schedule allows.

What decides the cost of duct repair in Chicago?

Access first, then scope. Reaching a joint in an open basement is quick work. The same joint above a finished ceiling, in a tight crawlspace or inside a wall is not. Price then follows the number of connections opened and sealed, and whether sheet metal fittings or new flex must be fabricated. Replaced insulation and any added boots, registers or dampers move it as well. Older wrapped insulation that may contain asbestos stops the job until an abatement contractor has cleared it. City & Suburban prices duct repair upfront with no hidden fees and puts the exact price in writing before work begins. Wells Fargo Home Projects financing is available subject to credit approval.

Is a duct problem ever a safety issue and not only a comfort issue?

Sometimes, and the return side is the reason. A large return leak in a furnace or utility room can pull air away from the appliance vent. Combustion gases then spill into the house instead of rising up the flue. Warning signs include a sooty draft hood and heavy window condensation near the appliance. A carbon monoxide alarm, even one that sounds only while the blower runs, means leaving the building first and calling 911 from outside, then the gas utility. Illinois requires carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas under the Carbon Monoxide Alarm Detector Act (430 ILCS 135). A suspected venting problem belongs in the urgent group, not on next week's calendar. City & Suburban offers same-day service when the schedule allows.

What about ducts in a condo or a unit inside a shared building?

Condo work has a boundary. The ductwork and air handler inside a unit often belong to the unit owner, but the condominium declaration and governing documents decide it. Shafts, risers and chases shared with other units usually belong to the association, and need approval before anything is opened. That approval has to be in hand before a shared shaft is opened, which is why the paperwork often sets the date. City & Suburban works on in-unit ductwork across 13 Chicago neighborhoods and 8 suburbs. Brandi C., June 2026: “Carissa was great staying on top of my slow-replying HOA to get the insurance info processed before Rob showed up.”

Does duct repair in Chicago need a City permit?

A repair in kind usually does not. Sealing a seam, re-securing a branch or replacing a damaged length with the same size is work on an existing system. Altering the layout, adding new runs or changing out the furnace or air handler is different work. Those are the jobs that appear in City of Chicago permit records. Whether a permit applies, and who files it, is worth confirming with the City and the contractor. Repairs in kind and alterations also price differently, so the distinction is worth settling at the quote. City & Suburban gives a written price before work starts. If opening a run reveals concealed damage, the scope and price should be revised in writing and approved before extra work goes ahead.

How does a homeowner keep the same duct fault from coming back?

Three habits cover most repeats. Stored boxes, bikes and bins kept clear of flex runs prevent the crushing that throttles a branch in the first place. Filters changed on schedule stop the blower from pulling against a loaded filter and straining the seams behind it. Support straps at the spacing the duct maker specifies stop the slow sag that reopens a joint. One more step pays off before a remodel. Photograph the duct routes while the joists and chases are still open, so nobody guesses behind new drywall later. City & Suburban maintenance plan members get priority dispatch.

What changes after a duct repair is finished?

Results depend on the home, so measure rather than assume. Where access allows, airflow at the repaired register can be read before and after the repair, so the change is documented. The temperature spread between rooms may narrow, but branch length, returns and insulation also affect balance. Runtime depends on the heat load as well as duct losses, so sealing can reduce furnace minutes on a cold night, though the saving varies. A return side that leaks less can also load the air filter more slowly. If a room stays starved after the repair, the remaining restriction needs its own diagnosis. One room gets little air Book soon

Likely causes

  • A branch has separated at a joint.
  • A duct is crushed or sharply bent.
  • Furniture blocks the room opening.

Check safely first

  • Check that the room opening is unobstructed.
  • Compare airflow with a nearby room.
  • Note whether closing the door changes comfort.

What the technician does

The technician traces the weak branch and compares nearby rooms. Repair depends on whether air escapes, meets a restriction, or lacks a return path.

Accessible faults are simpler; concealed runs need an access assessment.

When to act: Book an airflow assessment.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838
Air escapes through a visible seam Book soon

Likely causes

  • The connection has worked loose.
  • An old seal has peeled away.
  • The adjoining sections are poorly supported.

Check safely first

  • Observe the seam from a safe standing position.
  • Note when escaping air is strongest.
  • Leave the joint visible for inspection.

What the technician does

The technician checks joint fit and support before sealing. Suitable duct sealant or rated sealing tape addresses leakage once the connection is secure.

The number of leaking joints and their accessibility determine the scope.

When to act: Arrange repair before covering the joint.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838
A duct hangs loose or has disconnected Call today

Likely causes

  • A connection has pulled apart.
  • A support has failed.
  • Nearby work disturbed the branch.

Check safely first

  • Photograph the separation without moving the duct.
  • Identify which rooms have lost airflow.
  • Keep people and stored items away from the loose section.
  • Avoid climbing or reaching into a concealed opening.
  • Do not disturb old wrapped duct insulation or paper tape in an older building; leave it for assessment.

What the technician does

The technician checks both ends, restores the connection, and addresses support. Sealing cannot bridge a missing connection or support a loose run.

Reconnection may be limited work; damaged ends can require a replacement section.

When to act: Schedule prompt service for the affected rooms.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838
Flex duct is flattened or sharply bent Book soon

Likely causes

  • Stored items compressed the run.
  • A tight bend restricts the passage.
  • A sagging section has lost support.

Check safely first

  • Remove nearby movable items without touching the duct.
  • Note where the run appears flattened.
  • Do not cut or pull the outer covering.

What the technician does

The technician checks the inner passage and outer covering. Torn or permanently crushed sections may need replacement, with routing and support that prevent another restriction.

The damaged length and room to correct the route affect the work.

When to act: Arrange inspection rather than squeezing it back into shape.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838
Dust returns around room openings Book soon

Likely causes

  • A return joint draws air from an unintended space.
  • Dust has collected near an opening.
  • Household dust comes from another source.

Check safely first

  • Note which rooms collect dust most quickly.
  • Check whether furniture covers a return opening.
  • Record any recent building work.

What the technician does

The technician checks accessible return joints and other dust sources. Dust alone does not prove a duct defect, and repair cannot eliminate all household dust.

Tracing the entry point comes before choosing a repair.

When to act: Book an assessment if dust persists or airflow changes.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838
Bills rise while rooms stay uneven Book soon

Likely causes

  • Supply air leaks before reaching the room.
  • A restricted branch delivers little air.
  • Weather or another system problem changed energy use.

Check safely first

  • Compare bills for similar weather periods.
  • List rooms that remain uncomfortable.
  • Note whether airflow changed suddenly.

What the technician does

The technician checks whether a duct fault explains the room pattern. Repair addresses confirmed leakage, but any bill change depends on other conditions.

Several small leaks can require more inspection than one visible break.

When to act: Request diagnosis before replacing heating equipment.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838
Ducts bang or rattle during operation Book soon

Likely causes

  • A loose section vibrates against its support.
  • Metal moves as pressure changes.
  • A restriction changes airflow through the run.

Check safely first

  • Note when the noise begins and stops.
  • Record the sound from an accessible room.
  • Observe visible movement without touching the run.
  • Do not wedge objects against the duct.

What the technician does

The technician separates loose connections from movement caused by airflow. Support may address vibration; pressure-related sounds call for investigation of the restriction.

Finding the source may take longer when sound travels through concealed runs.

When to act: Arrange service if the sound is new or worsening.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838
Rust or moisture appears on a duct Book soon

Likely causes

  • Persistent moisture affected the metal.
  • Condensation forms on the exterior.
  • Water arrived from a nearby building leak.

Check safely first

  • Record whether moisture appears during cooling.
  • Look for nearby water marks without opening walls.
  • Keep stored belongings away from damp areas.
  • Avoid scraping or coating the damaged surface.
  • Do not disturb old wrapped duct insulation or paper tape in an older building; leave it for assessment.

What the technician does

The technician checks duct condition and the moisture source. Sealing weakened metal leaves the damage unresolved; affected sections may need replacement.

The moisture source and extent of weakened material determine the sequence.

When to act: Arrange inspection before coating or concealing damage.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838
Airflow changed after remodeling Book soon

Likely causes

  • A branch was moved or disconnected.
  • A new partition changed the return path.
  • New finishes conceal a restricted section.

Check safely first

  • Compare the current room layout with the earlier layout.
  • List openings that were moved or covered.
  • Share any photographs taken before walls closed.
  • Keep existing access panels available for the visit.

What the technician does

The technician traces the altered route and nearby connections. Concealed vertical runs in balloon-frame houses may need access planning before the repair scope is clear.

Existing access and records of the alteration can reduce uncertainty.

When to act: Book an assessment before closing remaining access.

Book a visit Call (773) 238-3838

What matters while a duct repair visit is pending

  • •Keep supply and return openings clear of furniture and stored items.
  • •Leave visible damage accessible instead of hiding it with a temporary covering.
  • •Record which rooms changed and whether the problem affects heating, cooling, or both.
  • •A loose duct should stay undisturbed until its connection and support can be inspected.
  • •A room without usable heat needs prompt attention during Chicago cold weather.

Air leakage or a damaged connection? A leaking seam needs a sound joint beneath the seal. A disconnected or crushed run needs its shape and connection restored first. Covering either defect without checking the air path can leave the room problem unresolved.

Residential duct repair questions

How are leaking or disconnected ducts actually repaired?

Repair starts at the joints. Loose connections are refastened with sheet metal screws, then sealed with mastic or UL 181 listed foil tape, never cloth duct tape. A supply branch that has pulled off its takeoff collar gets the collar re-secured, or a new collar where the old one is damaged. A fresh mechanical connection goes in either way. Torn or missing insulation is replaced so the sealed joint stays dry and quiet. City & Suburban has NATE-certified technicians, and the repair method should match the duct material and connection type. Sealing is a repair, not a rebuild. A run that is crushed or badly undersized along most of its length needs new duct instead.

How is a duct leak actually found?

By measurement, not by a glance. A useful assessment reads airflow and air temperature at the register in the room that is complaining, then compares them with a room that heats normally. It reads static pressure across the air handler as well, because a leaking return and a clogged filter move that number in opposite directions. The branch is then traced seam by seam until the gap, the dropped collar or the flattened length shows itself. A concealed run inside a wall chase or above finished plaster cannot be cleared by eye, so an access point has to be opened. City & Suburban diagnoses before quoting, which puts the readings ahead of the repair price rather than after it.

Why do far rooms in a two-flat or bungalow stay cold while the furnace runs?

Distance and leakage, usually in that order. Many two-flats, greystones and bungalows were ducted long after the frame went up. Branches travel through balloon-frame wall chases, panned floor joists and old gravity trunks never meant for a blower. Every unsealed seam on that path bleeds heated air into a basement, crawlspace or exterior wall before the register sees it. A front bedroom at the end of a long flex run loses most of its airflow this way. Airflow read at the registers shows which branch is losing its share. That weak branch is then traced back to the trunk it leaves.

Do duct leaks raise a heating bill enough to notice?

Leaks cost twice. Air that escapes a supply joint in an unheated basement never reaches a room. The thermostat then keeps the blower and burner running longer than the heat load requires. Return leaks are worse per square inch, because the system then pulls cold basement air back across the furnace and dilutes what every register delivers. Rental buildings feel this first. Where the landlord supplies heat, the Chicago Heat Ordinance applies. It sets a minimum of 68 degrees from 8:30 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. The overnight minimum is 66 degrees, and both apply between September 15 and June 1 (Municipal Code 13-196-410). A system fighting its own duct losses struggles to hold that in January.

Can crushed or kinked flex duct be repaired, or does it have to be replaced?

Flex duct fails by shape. A kink at a sharp turn, a length squashed behind stored boxes, or a long sagging span all throttle airflow. The duct can look intact from the outside. A crushed inner liner cannot be restored, so the damaged length is cut out and replaced. The new piece is pulled straight and carried on wide straps at the spacing the manufacturer specifies. A torn outer jacket is a smaller fix that can be sealed in place. A flattened section is replaced rather than taped back into shape, and the new run is kept as straight as the joist bays allow.

Does repairing ducts cut down on household dust?

Often yes, because return-side gaps pull unfiltered dust straight into the air stream. Gaps at a return plenum, an unsealed filter slot or a panned joist return draw in dust, loose fiberglass and crawlspace air. That load travels straight past the filter and spreads room to room. Sealing the return side is the part of duct repair that shows up on furniture and shelves. Duct repair belongs alongside filtration and humidity equipment as indoor air quality work. Cleaning the inside of a duct is a separate service and will not fix a leaking return.

How can a homeowner tell a duct fault from a furnace fault?

The pattern of the complaint points one way or the other. Heat that is weak in every room points at the equipment, the filter or the blower. So does a system that short cycles and trips its limit switch. Heat that is normal in some rooms and absent in others, with the furnace running fine, points at the duct path. Whistling at the cabinet, a thump when the blower starts and warm basement joists are duct signs. City & Suburban repairs both furnaces and ductwork, so the diagnosis decides the work. Equipment faults are handled as heater repair rather than duct repair.

What happens on a duct repair visit, and how long does it take?

A useful duct repair visit starts in the room that is complaining and works back along its branch. Readings at the register and at the air handler should set the scope before anything is opened. How long the visit takes depends on access and the number of joints opened. On an exposed basement or crawlspace run, sealing seams, re-securing a dropped branch and swapping flex are reachable repairs. Work behind finished plaster, or a fitting that must be fabricated for an odd gravity trunk, may need a second trip. City & Suburban gives a written price before the work, and same-day appointments are available when the schedule allows.

What decides the cost of duct repair in Chicago?

Access first, then scope. Reaching a joint in an open basement is quick work. The same joint above a finished ceiling, in a tight crawlspace or inside a wall is not. Price then follows the number of connections opened and sealed, and whether sheet metal fittings or new flex must be fabricated. Replaced insulation and any added boots, registers or dampers move it as well. Older wrapped insulation that may contain asbestos stops the job until an abatement contractor has cleared it. City & Suburban prices duct repair upfront with no hidden fees and puts the exact price in writing before work begins. Wells Fargo Home Projects financing is available subject to credit approval.

Is a duct problem ever a safety issue and not only a comfort issue?

Sometimes, and the return side is the reason. A large return leak in a furnace or utility room can pull air away from the appliance vent. Combustion gases then spill into the house instead of rising up the flue. Warning signs include a sooty draft hood and heavy window condensation near the appliance. A carbon monoxide alarm, even one that sounds only while the blower runs, means leaving the building first and calling 911 from outside, then the gas utility. Illinois requires carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas under the Carbon Monoxide Alarm Detector Act (430 ILCS 135). A suspected venting problem belongs in the urgent group, not on next week's calendar. City & Suburban offers same-day service when the schedule allows.

What about ducts in a condo or a unit inside a shared building?

Condo work has a boundary. The ductwork and air handler inside a unit often belong to the unit owner, but the condominium declaration and governing documents decide it. Shafts, risers and chases shared with other units usually belong to the association, and need approval before anything is opened. That approval has to be in hand before a shared shaft is opened, which is why the paperwork often sets the date. City & Suburban works on in-unit ductwork across 13 Chicago neighborhoods and 8 suburbs. Brandi C., June 2026: “Carissa was great staying on top of my slow-replying HOA to get the insurance info processed before Rob showed up.”

Does duct repair in Chicago need a City permit?

A repair in kind usually does not. Sealing a seam, re-securing a branch or replacing a damaged length with the same size is work on an existing system. Altering the layout, adding new runs or changing out the furnace or air handler is different work. Those are the jobs that appear in City of Chicago permit records. Whether a permit applies, and who files it, is worth confirming with the City and the contractor. Repairs in kind and alterations also price differently, so the distinction is worth settling at the quote. City & Suburban gives a written price before work starts. If opening a run reveals concealed damage, the scope and price should be revised in writing and approved before extra work goes ahead.

How does a homeowner keep the same duct fault from coming back?

Three habits cover most repeats. Stored boxes, bikes and bins kept clear of flex runs prevent the crushing that throttles a branch in the first place. Filters changed on schedule stop the blower from pulling against a loaded filter and straining the seams behind it. Support straps at the spacing the duct maker specifies stop the slow sag that reopens a joint. One more step pays off before a remodel. Photograph the duct routes while the joists and chases are still open, so nobody guesses behind new drywall later. City & Suburban maintenance plan members get priority dispatch.

What changes after a duct repair is finished?

Results depend on the home, so measure rather than assume. Where access allows, airflow at the repaired register can be read before and after the repair, so the change is documented. The temperature spread between rooms may narrow, but branch length, returns and insulation also affect balance. Runtime depends on the heat load as well as duct losses, so sealing can reduce furnace minutes on a cold night, though the saving varies. A return side that leaks less can also load the air filter more slowly. If a room stays starved after the repair, the remaining restriction needs its own diagnosis. City & Suburban diagnoses before quoting any further work.

City & Suburban has been family-owned since 1952 and is run by Rob, the second generation of the founding family. NATE-certified technicians do the service work. The company holds a 4.98 average across 204 Google reviews, 4.9 from 251 reviews on Yelp, and an A+ rating with the BBB. Adam L. wrote in September 2025: “Been using Rob at City & Suburban for a few years now. Always professional, responds and comes out to my home quickly, fixes the issue, and charges a reasonable price for his services.”

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: Do duct leaks raise a heating bill enough to notice?
contentFields.value: Do duct leaks raise a heating bill enough to notice?

contentFields.label: P: Leaks cost twice. Air that escapes a supply joint in an unheated basement never reaches a
contentFields.value: Leaks cost twice. Air that escapes a supply joint in an unheated basement never reaches a room. The thermostat then keeps the blower and burner running longer than the heat load requires. Return leaks are worse per square inch, because the system then pulls cold basement air back across the furnace and dilutes what every register delivers. Rental buildings feel this first. Where the landlord supplies heat, the Chicago Heat Ordinance applies. It sets a minimum of 68 degrees from 8:30 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. The overnight minimum is 66 degrees, and both apply between September 15 and June 1 (Municipal Code 13-196-410). A system fighting its own duct losses struggles to hold that in January.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: Can crushed or kinked flex duct be repaired, or does it have to be replaced?
contentFields.value: Can crushed or kinked flex duct be repaired, or does it have to be replaced?

contentFields.label: P: Flex duct fails by shape. A kink at a sharp turn, a length squashed behind stored boxes, o
contentFields.value: Flex duct fails by shape. A kink at a sharp turn, a length squashed behind stored boxes, or a long sagging span all throttle airflow. The duct can look intact from the outside. A crushed inner liner cannot be restored, so the damaged length is cut out and replaced. The new piece is pulled straight and carried on wide straps at the spacing the manufacturer specifies. A torn outer jacket is a smaller fix that can be sealed in place. A flattened section is replaced rather than taped back into shape, and the new run is kept as straight as the joist bays allow.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: Does repairing ducts cut down on household dust?
contentFields.value: Does repairing ducts cut down on household dust?

contentFields.label: P: Often yes, because return-side gaps pull unfiltered dust straight into the air stream. Gap
contentFields.value: Often yes, because return-side gaps pull unfiltered dust straight into the air stream. Gaps at a return plenum, an unsealed filter slot or a panned joist return draw in dust, loose fiberglass and crawlspace air. That load travels straight past the filter and spreads room to room. Sealing the return side is the part of duct repair that shows up on furniture and shelves. Duct repair belongs alongside filtration and humidity equipment as indoor air quality work. Cleaning the inside of a duct is a separate service and will not fix a leaking return.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: How can a homeowner tell a duct fault from a furnace fault?
contentFields.value: How can a homeowner tell a duct fault from a furnace fault?

contentFields.label: P: The pattern of the complaint points one way or the other. Heat that is weak in every room
contentFields.value: The pattern of the complaint points one way or the other. Heat that is weak in every room points at the equipment, the filter or the blower. So does a system that short cycles and trips its limit switch. Heat that is normal in some rooms and absent in others, with the furnace running fine, points at the duct path. Whistling at the cabinet, a thump when the blower starts and warm basement joists are duct signs. City & Suburban repairs both furnaces and ductwork, so the diagnosis decides the work. Equipment faults are handled as heater repair rather than duct repair.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: What happens on a duct repair visit, and how long does it take?
contentFields.value: What happens on a duct repair visit, and how long does it take?

contentFields.label: P: A useful duct repair visit starts in the room that is complaining and works back along its
contentFields.value: A useful duct repair visit starts in the room that is complaining and works back along its branch. Readings at the register and at the air handler should set the scope before anything is opened. How long the visit takes depends on access and the number of joints opened. On an exposed basement or crawlspace run, sealing seams, re-securing a dropped branch and swapping flex are reachable repairs. Work behind finished plaster, or a fitting that must be fabricated for an odd gravity trunk, may need a second trip. City & Suburban gives a written price before the work, and same-day appointments are available when the schedule allows.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: What decides the cost of duct repair in Chicago?
contentFields.value: What decides the cost of duct repair in Chicago?

contentFields.label: P: Access first, then scope. Reaching a joint in an open basement is quick work. The same joi
contentFields.value: Access first, then scope. Reaching a joint in an open basement is quick work. The same joint above a finished ceiling, in a tight crawlspace or inside a wall is not. Price then follows the number of connections opened and sealed, and whether sheet metal fittings or new flex must be fabricated. Replaced insulation and any added boots, registers or dampers move it as well. Older wrapped insulation that may contain asbestos stops the job until an abatement contractor has cleared it. City & Suburban prices duct repair upfront with no hidden fees and puts the exact price in writing before work begins. Wells Fargo Home Projects financing is available subject to credit approval.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: Is a duct problem ever a safety issue and not only a comfort issue?
contentFields.value: Is a duct problem ever a safety issue and not only a comfort issue?

contentFields.label: P: Sometimes, and the return side is the reason. A large return leak in a furnace or utility
contentFields.value: Sometimes, and the return side is the reason. A large return leak in a furnace or utility room can pull air away from the appliance vent. Combustion gases then spill into the house instead of rising up the flue. Warning signs include a sooty draft hood and heavy window condensation near the appliance. A carbon monoxide alarm, even one that sounds only while the blower runs, means leaving the building first and calling 911 from outside, then the gas utility. Illinois requires carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas under the Carbon Monoxide Alarm Detector Act (430 ILCS 135). A suspected venting problem belongs in the urgent group, not on next week's calendar. City & Suburban offers same-day service when the schedule allows.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: Does duct repair in Chicago need a City permit?
contentFields.value: Does duct repair in Chicago need a City permit?

contentFields.label: P: A repair in kind usually does not. Sealing a seam, re-securing a branch or replacing a dam
contentFields.value: A repair in kind usually does not. Sealing a seam, re-securing a branch or replacing a damaged length with the same size is work on an existing system. Altering the layout, adding new runs or changing out the furnace or air handler is different work. Those are the jobs that appear in City of Chicago permit records. Whether a permit applies, and who files it, is worth confirming with the City and the contractor. Repairs in kind and alterations also price differently, so the distinction is worth settling at the quote. City & Suburban gives a written price before work starts. If opening a run reveals concealed damage, the scope and price should be revised in writing and approved before extra work goes ahead.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: How does a homeowner keep the same duct fault from coming back?
contentFields.value: How does a homeowner keep the same duct fault from coming back?

contentFields.label: P: Three habits cover most repeats. Stored boxes, bikes and bins kept clear of flex runs prev
contentFields.value: Three habits cover most repeats. Stored boxes, bikes and bins kept clear of flex runs prevent the crushing that throttles a branch in the first place. Filters changed on schedule stop the blower from pulling against a loaded filter and straining the seams behind it. Support straps at the spacing the duct maker specifies stop the slow sag that reopens a joint. One more step pays off before a remodel. Photograph the duct routes while the joists and chases are still open, so nobody guesses behind new drywall later. City & Suburban maintenance plan members get priority dispatch.

contentFields.label: SUMMARY: What changes after a duct repair is finished?
contentFields.value: What changes after a duct repair is finished?

contentFields.value: Results depend on the home, so measure rather than assume. Where access allows, airflow at the repaired register can be read before and after the repair, so the change is documented. The temperature spread between rooms may narrow, but branch length, returns and insulation also affect balance. Runtime depends on the heat load as well as duct losses, so sealing can reduce furnace minutes on a cold night, though the saving varies. A return side that leaks less can also load the air filter more slowly. If a room stays starved after the repair, the remaining restriction needs its own diagnosis.
